purpose: Search literal source text across Python files currently present in canonical LIVE state. This is repository-content discovery; search_artifacts remains architectural entity discovery.
parameters: search_term (string, optional): single-line literal substring; newline (\n) and carriage return (\r) are invalid input; no regex, fuzzy, semantic or vector matching.
limit (positive integer or null, default 20): maximum logical matches returned; null returns all matches in canonical Python scope. max_items is not an alias for limit.
case_sensitive (boolean, default false): false uses Unicode casefold matching; true requires exact casing.
allow_large_output (boolean, default false): approve output above 15360 UTF-8 bytes after confirmation preflight.
query (string, optional): alias for search_term. At least one of search_term or query must be supplied; when both are supplied, they must match exactly.
behavior: Only canonical Python modules are enumerated; excluded and non-canonical files are never walked or searched. Comments, docstrings, string/numeric literals and ordinary code are searchable because matching operates on source text read through contextor.core.source.read_source without persistent source index.
Results are ordered deterministically by repository-relative path and logical span. Repeated hits in one logical span produce one result with matched_lines.

A logical span of at most 20 lines returns content_mode=full and its complete normalized text. Larger spans return content_mode=line_map: every line number, full matched lines, and non-match previews capped at four tokens and 60 characters.

Large line maps include expand metadata for get_source_range with the exact file and span. total_matches is counted before limit and truncated means fewer logical matches were returned than total_matches.
freshness: Search fails closed when canonical state is unavailable, requires resync, or a selected canonical module is parse-stale. It does not mutate LIVE state.
errors: Empty or multi-line search input supplied through search_term or query (containing \n or \r), invalid limit (including boolean, zero or negative), or non-boolean flags return controlled JSON errors.
Outputs above 15360 UTF-8 bytes return compact confirmation_required without echoing the query or results; repeat the same call with allow_large_output=true.
usage_notes: Use for finding hardcoded values, messages, comments or docstrings when the defining file or symbol is unknown. Start with the default limit and expand only the relevant large logical span.
examples: search_source(repo_path, "109.9") finds the literal text only inside canonical Python files.
